title: Add visibility for transient ingress-proxy retry spikes during scale-down events
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Summary:
During a capacity scale-down event on 2026-01-16 we observed a transient but high-volume spike in request retries originating at the ingress-proxy layer. The spike did not surface on any console dashboards we rely on for rollout/health decisions because we lack aggregated, per-route retry instrumentation and rollup panels. As a result the incident duration stretched while the team diagnosed retry amplification versus application-level errors.

Observed impact:
- ~6 minutes of elevated end-to-end tail latency for a subset of tenants (95th and 99th token-latency increased).
- Request retry loops amplified backend load during scale-down windows, contributing to cascade throttling in one dedicated pool.
- No existing alert or dashboard tile showed a sustained retry ratio increase across routes — only low-level proxy logs contained the signal.

Root cause hypothesis:
The autoscaler triggered scale-down of a small number of inference workers. Conn reset / connection churn during the drain window caused the ingress-proxy to retry requests. Because retries were not attributed with both original-request-id and route/tenant labels in metrics, retries looked like new requests in some charts and were invisible as a correlated signal across ingress -> runtime. Tracing sampling rates were low for the ingress-proxy during non-incident windows so we did not have enough traces to reconstruct retry chains quickly.

Why this is a blind spot for Console/Observability:
- No metric with the shape: ingress.retry_count{route,tenant,reason} emitted at ingestion/edge.
- No rollup panel showing retry-rate / retry-ratio (retries per original-req) with p50/p95/p99 across tenants and routes.
- Traces do not consistently include retry loop span annotations and a shared request_id tag to join retry attempts.
- Alerts only consider 5xx percentages and latency; they do not trigger on increased retry ratio that precedes backend 5xx in these scenarios.

Proposed remediation work (this ticket):
1) Instrumentation (edge): emit a counter metric ingress.retry_total with labels {route, tenant_id, reason, proxied=true} and an associated gauge ingress.inflight_retries for real-time panels. Ensure metric cardinality is capped by using normalized route names and hashed tenant_id when needed.
2) Tracing: add a lightweight span to the ingress-proxy that annotates "retry_attempt" with attempt index and includes original_request_id header (propagate across retries). Increase sampling to 2% for ingress component for 15m after rollout events and during autoscaler actions via temporary sampling config.
3) Dashboards: Add a new console tile under "Edge Health" showing retry_ratio = ingress.retry_total / ingress.request_total with time-series and heatmap by tenant. Add per-route panels for p50/p95 retry_ratio and a table listing top-20 tenants by observed retries in the last 5 minutes.
4) Alerts: Create an alert "HighRetryRatio" (P0 for 5min sustained > 1% at org level OR > 0.25% for any tenant with >10k reqs/min) and a higher-severity alert for sustained growth during scale operations. Wire to on-call playbook.
5) Canary & Runbook: Add a synthetic canary that simulates a scale-down and validates retry_ratio returns to baseline within 60s. Update incident runbook with mitigation steps: extend proxy drain timeout, enable short-circuit backoff for control-plane requests, and trigger temporary sampling increase.

Acceptance criteria:
- ingress.retry_total (and retry_ratio panels) are recorded and visible in Console for the last 30 days.
- Trace spans include original_request_id and attempt index for >90% of sampled retries.
- New dashboard tile shows retry_ratio by tenant and route, and is included in the default "Edge Health" dashboard.
- HighRetryRatio alert is created, tested with a firehose replay, and page rules validated with runbook steps.
- Post-deployment: for the next two scale operations, retry_ratio remains below historical incident spike thresholds and any regression triggers the new alert.

Rollout plan and risk mitigation:
- Implement metric + trace changes behind a feature flag in ingress-proxy; deploy to staging and a small percentage of edge hosts first.
- After verifying metric shape and dashboards in staging, enable in 20% prod hosts; monitor increased metrics volume and cardinality impact for 48 hours.
- If metric cardinality grows, fallback by switching tenant labels to hashed buckets (10k buckets).

Owner and stakeholders:
- Owner: Omar Castillo (edge/sre)
- Secondary: Lina Chen (observability)
- Reviewers: Console UX (Priya Raman), Runtime infra (Maxwell Ito), SRE on-call (team rotation)

Estimated effort: ~5 story points.

Links and references: see attachments for dashboard prototypes, a short demo video, and a draft runbook.
comments: 2026-01-16 — Lina Chen: Initial incident report: observed bursty retries at 16:04 UTC during a scheduled scale-down. Triage indicates retries at ingress level; file created to track follow-up work.

2026-01-17 — Omar Castillo: Confirmed lack of retry rollup in Console. Captured example proxy logs and exported CSV for repro; creating metric proposal and spike dashboard mockup (link in attachments).
2026-01-20 — Priya Raman: UX reviewed dashboard mockup. Recommend an aggregated heatmap and per-tenant drilldown rather than too many small panels. Agreed to include top-20 tenant table.

2026-01-23 — Maxwell Ito: Runtime confirmed that retries show up as new requests downstream; suggested adding original_request_id propagation and a retry_attempt header. Noted caution on header size; prefer short opaque id.
2026-01-28 — Omar Castillo: Prototype metric added behind flag. Staging telemetry looks correct; sending PR for tracing changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/pull/1284

2026-02-01 — QA (Aisha Patel): Smoke tests run in staging. Metrics appear in Console, but top-20 table requires an additional index on tenant_id for query speed. Filed follow-up backend ticket ENG-101289 to add index.
2026-02-02 — Omar Castillo: Merged metric PR to canary fleet. Monitoring for cardinality and volume; updating this ticket once alerts are created and runbook validated.
